tfn.s: Sleep trackers always measure sleep perfectly.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "But the numbers are not always perfectly accurate."

tfn.s: Orthosomnia is an official diagnosis for everyone who uses a watch.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "The term describes a pattern of behaviour discussed in clinical reports; it is not an official diagnosis for everyone who uses a watch."

tfn.s: Most people stop using their sleep tracker within a year.
tfn.why: Not stated. This version does not give this information.

tfn.s: A tracker can show you that you go to bed at very different times.
tfn.why: The text says: "They can help us work out our habits, such as going to bed at very different times."

match.d: able to make you believe something

items.s: Seeing a low number can make someone feel ____ before breakfast.

tfn.s: A low score can make someone worry about a problem they had not noticed.
tfn.why: The text says: "Someone who checks a score immediately after waking might begin the day worrying about a problem they would otherwise not have noticed."

tfn.s: The term orthosomnia appeared in a 2017 article in the Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine.
tfn.why: The text says: "Researchers described the term orthosomnia in a 2017 article in the Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine."

tfn.s: Doctors now advise patients to stop using sleep trackers altogether.
tfn.why: Not stated. This version does not give this information.

tfn.s: Consumer devices measure sleep as accurately as a medical assessment does.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "Their reports can be useful for spotting patterns, yet they are not equivalent to a medical sleep assessment."

more than is reasonable or necessary

tfn.s: The text recommends giving up sleep technology completely.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "Yet dismissing sleep technology entirely would be excessive."

tfn.s: Sleep trackers are more popular with younger users than with older ones.
tfn.why: Not stated. This version does not give this information.

tfn.s: A precise-looking number can hide doubt about when somebody was awake.
tfn.why: The text says: "A number displayed with apparent precision can conceal uncertainty about when a person was awake or how accurately particular sleep stages were identified."

tfn.s: The 2017 paper proved that sleep tracking causes insomnia.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "Their observations were case reports, not evidence that tracking routinely causes insomnia or that orthosomnia is a universally recognised medical diagnosis."
